Category: Abstract.

spec.name: Animaris Ventus — Wind-Walking Strandbeest
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style kinetic beach creature: a pale-yellow PVC tube lattice spine standing on four triangulated tube legs, topped with a wind-catching yellow sail rig, a front rotor wind-organ and a ruddered tail.
spec.layout: A wind-walking tube animal built entirely from cylinders-as-tubes, flat membranes and small fittings; nothing is smoothed, every joint is a visible coupling disc or zip-tie collar. From the front (+Z): a circular wind rotor (a ring of 8 flat paddle blades on a tube A-frame, hub at [0, 2.0, 2.1]) reads as the head. Behind it the hull is a shallow rectangular tube truss: two parallel top rails at x = ±0.28 arcing from y 1.52 at the front to y 1.62 mid-body down to y 1.45 at the rear, over lower rails at y 1.08, cross-rung every ~0.4 m from z -2.1 to z 1.85, with thin diagonal braces; a mid keel tube runs under the top rails. The four legs are the signature: at each hip mount [±0.55, 1.08, z] (front z 1.05, rear z -1.35) a lattice of yellow PVC tubes — thigh out to the knee [±0.95, 0.70, z+0.18], shank back down to the ankle [±0.72, 0.16, z-0.05], and a straight top strut hip-to-ankle closing the triangle — plus one secondary brace and a flat triangular shin web plate; each leg ends in a wide dark foot pad flat on the sand with three transverse teal grip bars. Above the mid-deck a mast rises from [0, 1.6, 0.1] to [0, 2.5, 0.1] carrying two triangular yellow sails (a forward one to a bow spreader at [0, 2.15, 1.1], an aft one to [0, 2.2, -1.2]), each with three tube battens, ink edge seams, and two horizontal wing spars reaching to x = ±1.0 at y 2.2 with small hanging membrane panels and thin ink guy lines. At the rear, two tail tubes drop back from [0, 1.7, -2.15] to [±0.15, 1.35, -2.55] braced by a cross strut, carrying a vertical sail-cloth rudder fin (peaking at y 2.5 around z -2.4) with a small orange pennant at its top and thin ink steering drag-lines running forward to the rear hips. The only parts touching y = 0 are the four foot pads; everything else stands above. Style on every part: pale PVC yellow tubes with white coupling discs and dark zip-tie collars at every connection, yellow sail cloth, dark feet and hardware, a single orange-red accent for the pennant and blade tips, small teal details — flat colours throughout, low-poly, joints and struts slightly oversized so the machine reads as a walking skeleton.

parts.builds: The main tube truss that everything else hangs from. Two parallel top rails (tubes radius ~0.035) at x = ±0.28 running from z 1.85 to z -2.1, each arcing gently: y 1.52 at the front, rising to 1.62 around z 0.3, easing to 1.45 at the rear; sweep them as smooth tube sweeps in pvc with a few pvcShade coupling sleeves. Two lower rails at x = ±0.28, y 1.08, same z range, in pvcShade. Cross-rung tubes every ~0.4 m of z connecting top to lower rails on both sides (pvc), plus a central keel tube at x = 0, y 1.05 running z 1.6 to -1.9. Thin diagonal brace tubes (radius 0.018, pvcShade) zig-zagging between rungs on each side for the lattice look. At every rail-rung intersection place a small bone-coloured coupling disc (short cylinder radius 0.055, thickness 0.02) and, on about one third of them, an ink zip-tie collar ring (torus or short cylinder radius 0.045) for the taped-together look. Four hip socket brackets of bone colour where the hip mounts sit: short horizontal tube stubs from the rails out to each hipFL/hipFR/hipBL/hipBR mount point, ending in a coupling disc the leg part builds onto. Bow: the front rails converge toward spineF with a transverse bumper tube at z 1.85. No mast, sails, rotor or tail here — those belong to their own parts; end the rails cleanly at the head and tail mounts.
parts.attaches: Owns the spine skeleton: rails hang on core, spineF and spineB. Delivers the hip socket brackets at mounts hipFL, hipFR, hipBL, hipBR for the legs part, the bow convergence toward spineF/rotorHub for the head part, the mastBase seating at the top of the truss around z 0.1 for the sails part, and the clean rail ends at spineB/tailRoot for the tail part.

parts.builds: All four walking legs, identical in construction, mirrored left/right, front pair slightly longer-strided than rear pair. Each leg builds from its hip mount (hipFL/hipFR/hipBL/hipBR): a hip coupling cluster (bone-coloured disc radius 0.07 plus an ink zip collar), then the Strandbeest triangle in pvc tubes radius 0.03 — thigh from hip to knee mount, shank from knee to ankle mount, and a straight top strut closing hip to ankle; plus one secondary thin brace (pvcShade radius 0.018) from mid-thigh to mid-shank, and a thin flat triangular shin web plate (sailDeep, thickness ~0.008, seated inside the triangle between the three struts) as the membrane panel every Animaris shin carries. At the knee: a bone coupling disc radius 0.06 on both sides of the joint with an ink zip collar. At the ankle: a smaller bone disc radius 0.05. Each leg ends in a foot pad: a flat ink-coloured rounded box or squashed cylinder ~0.34 wide (x) × 0.05 tall × 0.5 long (z), centred under its ankle so its underside sits exactly on y = 0, with three transverse teal grip bars (thin boxes across the pad top) and one small pvcShade strap tube over the ankle. Optional character detail per leg: a hand-written number tag (a small bone-coloured plate) on the shin web — front legs 1/2, rear legs 3/4. Keep all tube ends tucked into couplings so no tube floats free; the triangle silhouettes must read clearly from the side.
parts.attaches: Builds onto the hip socket brackets at mounts hipFL, hipFR, hipBL, hipBR and rides the leg chains hipFL/kneeFL/ankleFL (and FR, BL, BR). The foot pads are the only floor contact of the whole model: their undersides rest exactly on y = 0.

parts.builds: The wind-catching rig above the deck. A central mast tube (pvc radius 0.045) from mount mastBase [0, 1.6, 0.1] up to mastTop [0, 2.5, 0.1], with a bone collar at the base and an ink zip ring at mid-height. Two triangular sails of sail-coloured membrane with sailDeep shading on their aft faces: a forward sail from the mast (spanning y 2.4 down to 1.75) out to a bow spreader tube tip at [0, 2.15, 1.1], and an aft sail out to [0, 2.2, -1.2]; give each sail three pvcShade tube battens crossing it horizontally (radius 0.015) and an ink seam tube along its trailing edge. From the mast at y 2.2, two horizontal wing spars (pvc radius 0.028) reach out to x = ±1.0; from each spar hang two small rectangular membrane panels (sail, sailDeep lower half, ink hem) like the flapping wing mats of a strandbeest, and a thin ink guy line runs from each spar tip diagonally down to the deck rails around z -0.4. Top the mast with a small bone cap and a short orange accent pennant tube at the very tip. Sails should read as taut flat cloth — flat membranes, no sag geometry — with the battens clearly seated on the surface.
parts.attaches: The mast seats at mount mastBase on the spineHull truss and rides joints mastTop and spineF. Spar guy lines land on the spineHull deck rails; nothing reaches into the head or tail boxes.

parts.builds: The head of the machine: a wind rotor on an A-frame. The frame: two pvc tubes radius 0.03 rising from the front rail ends of the hull near spineF (around [±0.28, 1.55, 1.7]) converging to the rotorHub mount [0, 2.0, 2.1], cross-braced by one horizontal tube between them at y 1.75 and one diagonal each side (pvcShade), all ends in bone couplings. The rotor itself rides the rotorHub joint: a steel axle stub along z (radius 0.02, length 0.3), a bone hub disc radius 0.09 with an ink centre bolt, a shallow torus-like rim ring of pvc tube radius 0.52 around the axle plane (build it as a swept tube along a circle, 8-10 segments so it stays low-poly), and 8 flat paddle blades between hub and rim — thin steel plates ~0.06 × 0.4 with accent-coloured tip caps (small boxes), each blade set at a slight pitch angle so the fan reads as a wind organ; phase the blades evenly. Behind the rotor, two short antennae tubes from the frame top spread in a V (pvc radius 0.015) with tiny teal pennant flags (small flat quads) at their tips, and a small bone-coloured nameplate on the frame cross tube. The rotor, frame and antennae are the whole head: no face, the machine's character is the fan.
parts.attaches: The A-frame feet land on the spineHull front rails around spineF and its apex carries the rotor at mount rotorHub, riding joints spineF and rotorHub. Its rear face stays clear of the sailRig box except along the shared boundary at z 1.85.

parts.builds: The rear assembly: steering tail and rudder. From mount tailRoot [0, 1.7, -2.15]: two pvc tubes radius 0.03 angling down and back to [±0.15, 1.35, -2.55], joined by a horizontal cross tube at their tips and one diagonal brace back to the hull's rear rails (pvcShade), all with bone couplings and ink zip collars. Rising between them, a vertical rudder fin: a flat sailDeep membrane/plate in the shape of a swept-back fin, roughly 0.55 long (z) and 0.8 tall, from y 1.45 up to a peak at y 2.5 around z -2.4, with an ink edge seam tube along its top and trailing edges and one pvcShade batten across it. A short orange pennant flag (small flat quad) flies from the fin peak on a stub mast. Two thin ink steering drag-lines run from the fin's lower corners forward along the hull sides to near mounts hipBL/hipBR, as slack-curved thin tubes (radius 0.008). A small bone tail-light disc on the fin's rear face finishes it.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount tailRoot on the spineHull rear rail convergence, riding joints spineB and tailRoot. The drag-lines reach forward along the hull sides toward mounts hipBL/hipBR but stay clear of the leg boxes except at their endpoints.

calls.reasoning:
Let me design a Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture beach creature — a Strandbeest. Made of tubes: PVC-like tube frame, wind sail/wings, articulated legs with lots of joints, walking on the beach.

Key features: a wind-driven creature with a spine of tubes, multiple leg pairs (bipedal gait like Strandbeests), a sail/propeller assembly, wing-like spines, a long neck/head maybe. Style: pale PVC yellow-white tubes, zip ties, PET bottle wings? Classic Strandbeest: yellow PVC pipes (often yellow/orange), plastic sheets (yellow sails), and the "Animaris" name.

Structure:
- Central spine tube running along z, elevated ~1.6m.
- Two large sail wings / wind sail on a wind organ top.
- Many legs (two pairs visible: 2 legs, maybe 4) with triangular PVC linkage frames — those are the signature: leg assemblies built of triangles of tube.
- A front "head" with wind organ / rotor.

Size: maybe 2.4 wide, 2.6 high, 5 long. Legs must touch floor.

Plan joints: spine chain (root spine joints along body), head/wind organ hub, legs as chains (leg chains with roles), sail hinge, tail. Keep joints reasonable: legs 4 legs × 4 joints = 16, spine 4, neck 2, tail 2, sail 2, rotor 1. Under 160 easily.

Let me define the skeleton:

- root "core" at [0, 1.15, 0.3] dir up... Actually root spine. Let's do a spine chain: joints body0..body3 along z from front to back at height ~1.5.

Spec format requires joints listed with at/dir/role/parent. Parts build on those joints.

Parts (4-6):
1. "spine" — the central hull: parallel tube rails connected with cross-braces, spine cage. Box: full length, centered.
2. "legs" — 4 leg assemblies, triangular PVC linkage, feet on floor. Each leg: hip mount at spine bottom, knee triangle, ankle, flat foot. floor: true for legs.
3. "sails" — the wind sail / wing assembly on top: a tall mast with a membrane sail + horizontal wind-organ rotor blades at front? Or propeller wings. Signature: yellow plastic sails with batten ribs.
4. "head" — front: wind organ rotor (turbofan of tube spokes), beak/handle bar.
5. "tail" — rear rudder fin / tail tubes + steering bars.

Maybe 5 parts. Budget: total ~ 900; budgets like spine 180, legs 260, sails 200, head 150, tail 110 = 900.

Colors: PVC pale yellow "#e8d55a"? Real Strandbeests: yellow-ish PVC tubes, plastic bottle sails yellow/white, zip ties black. Palette:
- tube: "#e6c94f" (pale yellow PVC)
- tubeDark: "#c9a92e" (shaded joints)
- sail: "#f4e886" lighter yellow translucent
- sailDeep: "#d9b83a"
- ink: "#2a2a30" (zip ties, joints, feet pads, cam)
- accent: "#e8542e" (orange-red tips, warning flag)
- bone: "#f2ecd9" white joints
- maybe teal accent "#2b8a8f" small flags.

Mounts:
- spineHull: top rail line at y=1.55
- hipFrontL/R etc. Legs attach at hips: front hip mounts at [±0.55, 1.05, 1.2] and rear [±0.55, 1.05, -1.4].
- mastBase [0, 1.75, 0.1]
- rotorHub [0, 2.0, 2.05]
- tailRoot [0, 1.5, -2.3]

Joints: skeleton list:
- root: "core" at [0, 1.2, 0.2], dir [0,0,1]? role spine. Actually make spine a chain of joints: "spine1".."spine4" along z. Simpler: individual joints each with parent.

Joints (order, parents first):
1. core [0,1.25,0.2] dir [0,0,1] role spine (root)
2. spineF [0,1.5,1.3] parent core dir [0,0,1] role spine
3. spineB [0,1.45,-1.5] parent core dir [0,0,-1] role spine
4. spineT [0,1.6,-2.3] parent spineB dir [0,0.15,-1] role tail — tail root
5. hipsF [0,1.05,1.15] parent spineF dir [0,-1,0] role hinge? Legs attach here. Actually legs need joints themselves. Let each part create its own leg chain joints? Spec says joints created in this order before any part runs. So list leg joints too. But that's a lot. Alternative: each part lists joints from the shared skeleton; part builders create sub-joints (chains) themselves? The instructions: "joints is the skeleton, created in this order before any part runs". Part lists joints it rides. Probably sub-joints can be created by part builders (chain building via b.chain inside parts). To be safe, put main skeleton in the joints list and let leg part build its own chains with b.chain parented to hip mounts. But builder spec says each builder only has shared spec... they know SDK, can create chains with parent joint names. I'll specify in each part which joints they create. Actually the spec format only has "joints": ["body"] list of which shared joints geometry rides. I can note in the part's "builds" that it creates its own chains. Risky for duplication — better to define all joints in the shared list so builders don't invent conflicting ones.

Define leg joints: 4 legs × 3 joints (hip, knee, ankle) = 12 joints. Names: hipFL, kneeFL, ankleFL, etc. role "leg" for chain? role per joint: hip/knee/ankle → role "leg". Feet as tip at ankle dir down.

Legs geometry: Strandbeest legs are triangular lattice: thigh tube from hip, a horizontal linkage, shank to ankle, and a big triangular sail-like shin plate. Simplify: hip at [±0.55, 1.05, z], knee forward-out at [±0.8, 0.75, z+0.25], ankle at [±0.7, 0.18, z], foot flat on floor y=0. Feet: wide pads.

I'll do: a top spine ridge at y=2.3 carrying pairs of horizontal wing sails extending outward ±X with tube ribs and membrane, from z 0.8 to -1.6. That's the "walk along wind wings".

Tail: rear: rudder fin (vertical flat fin) + tail tubes trailing + an orange flag.

Legs: Strandbeest legs have a distinctive triangular shin with a fan of struts and a flat "foot" — I'll describe: each leg a lattice of tubes: hip post, thigh tube going down-back, knee triangle, shank to ankle, cross strut, plus flat foot pad (dark) with sand grip bars. - mastTop [0,2.5,0.1] parent spineF dir [0,1,0] role spine (for sails).
